newsitem.title: UK: Cadbury down as Q1 U.S. sales disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Cadbury down as Q1 U.S. sales disappoint.

text.p: Shares in British food and drinks group Cadbury Schweppes Plc fell back on Wednesday after it announced soft drinks sales figures for the U.S. in the first quarter, dealers said.
Cadbury Schweppes' shares were down seven pence, or 1.34 percent, to 516.5p by 0945 GMT in volume of 1.9 million while the FTSE-100 index was 4.5 points, or 0.10 percent, higher at 4,437.7.
"The Dr Pepper figures weren't good enough after the Pepsi report yesterday (Tuesday)," a marketmaker at a British bank said.

Cadbury Schweppes Plc said volume sales of soft drinks in the U.S. rose one percent in the first quarter. Volume sales of its Dr Pepper brand rose five percent, while sales of its 7 Up and other brands dropped by two percent.

A Cadbury spokeswoman said soft drinks sales in the Americas accounted for around 60 percent of the group's beverage sales worldwide. The Americas accounted for just under 30 percent of total group beverage and confectionery sales.
Cadbury is third in the U.S. soft drinks market to Coca-Cola and PepsiCo Inc.
On Tuesday, PepsiCo reported an eight percent rise in earnings for the first quarter, led by strong North American sales of Pepsi and Mountain Dew soft drinks.
Case sales grew six percent, driven by double-digit volume growth for Mountain Dew and solid growth in Pepsi, the company said.
